facts.text: Lacey was originally called Woodland after settlers Isaac and Catherine Wood, who claimed land there in 1853.
Lacey’s first library began in a school basement in the 1930s, moved to Market Square in 1966, and opened the Timberland Regional Library in 1991.
Seven historical markers in Lacey, including one for the Lacey Depot, sit along the Karen Fraser Woodland Trail near the train station.
South Sound Center, Lacey’s largest retail area, opened in 1966 as an enclosed mall before becoming an open‑air shopping center in 2000.
Lacey’s Alternative Energy Initiative powers all city buildings, parks, and 3,000 streetlights with 100% green electricity and plans electric vehicle charging stations.
The historic Kluh Clock, donated to Lacey in 2001, stands as a noted landmark at South Sound Center.
